---
name: cis-agent-execution
description: Execute one approved CIS task through a discovered Codex or Claude provider with explicit modes, permissions, isolation, durable provenance, cancellation, resumption, and result reconciliation.
---

# CIS agent execution

1. Run `cis repo init --root <documentation-root>` when required. If initialization or command discovery fails, run `cis repo doctor` before retrying.
2. For pre-change BRD work, use `cis agent author brd` only with explicitly selected references. Then use `cis agent review brd` with a different provider, review mode, and read-only isolation; include extracted authoring evidence only after explicit disclosure authority. For delivery work, read `docs/references/agent-provider-profile.md`, the approved change plan, the selected ready task, and repository delivery policy.
3. Run `cis agent providers --format agent` and `cis agent provider diagnose <provider> --format agent`; provider availability never grants authority.
4. Run `cis agent prepare <change-id> <task-id> --provider <provider> --format agent` and inspect the bound digest and permission ceiling.
5. Run `cis agent run` with required provider, mode, permission and actor; select target and transport when needed. This command has no `--reason` option; retain rationale with the task. Workspace-write defaults to an isolated Git worktree whose baseline includes current tracked and non-ignored untracked changes.
6. Use `--approve-requests` only for explicitly authorized supported Codex requests within its declared ceiling. For Claude implementation tasks with workspace-write, optionally repeat `--allow-command` for reviewed literal commands. These native rules apply to one attempt, not read-only or document-authoring runs. They add permissions, not a shell/filesystem sandbox; native normalization, compound commands, directory changes and build-script effects remain relevant. A denied command is a failed attempt, not a waiting approval dialog.
7. Inspect durable state with `cis agent runs` and `cis agent show`; cancel with an actor and reason. Use `recover` only for a proven orphaned process before an explicit `resume`. A resumed attempt never erases the first attempt. Resume requires an explicit actor and reason. Supply any command list again; CIS restarts native session context when either attempt has a list. Retain actual tool outputs, not just the model's success claim.
8. Inspect the structured result before `cis agent import-result`. Imported output is evidence only; it cannot approve plans, accept designs, complete tasks, or verify delivery.

Where adopted engineering defaults (`requireTaskCompletion: true`) or existing authority-owned accounting govern direct plan/task runs and story work, inspect the canonical owner's `cis agent work status <change-id> --task <task-id>`. Resolve a missing allocation through `cis agent work allocate <change-id> --input <allocation.json> --actor <authorized-controller> --reason <allocation-rationale>` using actual authorized task/change limits, reserve, decision and storage references, and an explicit acknowledgment of unmeasured historical effort. An exact registered owned participant's controls permit allocation at its authority; retained story correction history also permits explicit finite allocation against existing approved canonical work.

Establishing that allocation adopts work accounting across the authority. Every supported direct-task and story route then needs its canonical owner and applicable finite allocation, including sibling tasks without correction history or engineering quality policy. One task's allocation grants no capacity to another. This does not adopt engineering quality policy or grant plan, design or completion approval. Reconcile the displayed historical effort before reusing those runs or granting a specific bounded correction. A provider profile, model output, new run ID, resume reason, or `--approve-requests` cannot grant or reset allocation. Missing or corrupt adopted accounting requires reconciliation. Authorities without adopted accounting or applicable engineering defaults retain their non-adopted execution boundaries. Product-document authoring and import operations retain their dedicated flows.

Record one concise checkpoint through `cis agent work progress <change-id> <task-id> --input <checkpoint.json> --actor <controller>` at the first useful result and before broadening work. At the next safe admission boundary, cumulative active work reaching the adopted execution window (3,600 seconds in the reviewed profile, or an applicable narrower window) holds further expensive work until qualifying controller progress is recorded. Preserve Outcome / nonempty Evidence / measured Cost / Approach / Decision and the next bounded action; use current revisions and existing evidence. Automatic settlement or disposition summaries, status reads and model success claims do not qualify. Routine reflection may keep `closeAttempt: false` and continue the same logical attempt without another reviewer, human approval, or canonical task `Blocked` transition; all independent holds remain. Two logical attempts with the same blocker and no material new information hold unchanged expensive repetition; expected failing development tests do not count automatically. Use `cis agent work disposition` with a supported justified in-scope simplification or continuation under existing delegation, preserving spent work, hard limits, recovery uncertainty, and actual approval/permission gates.

Ordinary allocation redistribution cannot reduce protected task restoration reserves; repeat an existing reserve on update, because omitting it as zero is rejected when a nonzero reserve exists. For interrupted preparation, `work disposition reconcile` requires verified stopped ownership of the original preparing controller as well as its grace period. A live, other-host, unreadable or missing historical owner stays held; elapsed time and no provider PID alone prove nothing. Cancellation validates the bounded retained manifest/event/accounting evidence and can stop an independently verified live owned process despite uncertainty about another identity. Unverifiable processes remain untargeted; partial cleanup returns non-success and retains the reservation until every relevant owned identity is resolved and stopped. Preserve actor/reason, repository/run validation, evidence checks and recorded terminal provenance. Read the `cis agent work`, `cancel` and `recover` manuals for complete headless inputs and safe continuation.

When story reflection is due, `story work-status` reports `controller-assessment-required`. As the authorized orchestrating agent, inspect retained implementation, failed/valid review evidence, measured cost, reservations, remaining capacity and current revision. Record Outcome, nonempty Evidence, Approach, Decision and the next bounded action through `cis agent work progress <change-id> <task-id> --input <assessment.json> --actor <controller>` at the existing canonical owner; CIS supplies measured Cost. Keep `closeAttempt: false` unless the logical attempt has ended, then resume the same governed story with refreshed tokens. No routine human acknowledgment, extra reviewer or task `Blocked` transition is needed. Automatic `story-execution-summary` and legacy `story-controller-progress` records never qualify, and candidate reuse cannot refresh reflection credit. Explicit controller progress remains the existing owner-wide assessment route; incidental story summaries cannot satisfy direct-task reflection. Status reads record nothing; independent holds and counters remain binding.

For story work, inspect `cis brd feature wizard story status` and its delivery-size assessment, task contract and blocking reasons. Use explicit `assess`, `decompose` and `prepare --input` proposals as documented in the wizard-status manual; reading status never prepares work. Unknown/stale or above-medium delivery needs assessment or bounded child outcomes before implementation. A bounded sensitive task may still require high reasoning strength and independent review. Preserve instance IDs, work-owner links and exact prerequisites; use the resolved category, outputs, criteria and verification obligations for both implementation and review. Inspect `story work-status` for the existing canonical owner and shared allowance; where that association is missing, use `story bind-work --input` with current story tokens and an existing approved change/task, then allocate at that owner once. Authority or participant adoption cannot be bypassed through an unconfigured target. Implementation, review, correction, retry and linked-repository stages retain the same owner and logical attempt; reused work retains its historical cost. Generic `agent resume` redirects a story stage to its governed story continuation instead of running synthetic stage IDs as direct tasks.

Governed story correction history retains two automatic correction rounds across invocations. Correct required findings only; optional advice remains visible without compulsory changes or answers. New task reviews state required/optional disposition and supporting basis independently of severity. Ready with required findings, or revise/blocked with only optional advice, is inconsistent evidence. At the correction limit, inspect the retained relationship/findings and use a relevant authorized `agent work disposition` for one bounded next step within remaining capacity; it never grants two fresh rounds. Routine progress and justified simplification proceed under existing delegation while hard capacity, recovery, permission and approval holds remain.

A granted correction carries its authorized hypothesis, specific next action and disposition provenance into the actual correction and independent-review requests. Recovery and extensions retain prior direction, round identity, compatible stages and spent work. Missing pre-fix direction must come from the exact retained authorized disposition or the reported bounded `simplify` reconciliation; never invent it or use a generic continuation. Nested stages created by the governed story or correction controller use only the admitted parent's remaining whole seconds, rounded down within parent/correction deadlines, including fewer than 30; preparation stays charged. Direct `cis agent run` requests, including `--parent-execution`, and new root requests retain the 30-second minimum; direct requests must fit the parent's remainder without automatic shortening. An early failure before a new review preserves legacy findings and still-current saved responses; material changes still require assessment, and an explicitly empty newer review supersedes obsolete findings. Answers do not waive defects or approve completion.

When actual work materially expands verification machinery, record the necessary invariant, adopted native alternative, existing measured/estimated/unknown cost, maintenance/pass-semantics effect and duplication avoided in the existing independent review. Ordinary helpers and assertions require no additional ceremony or benchmark. Obtain `completion-context`, retain actual current evidence and use `complete` only when all applicable obligations and existing approval gates pass. Story implementation records retain their authority location; story review receipts use hash-verified participant copies of the retained read-only run as documented in story completion evidence.

Never copy provider credentials into CIS, infer permission from tool availability, run a non-ready task, bypass the design barrier for downstream work, or treat an agent's completion claim as canonical CIS state. Coordination, wireframe, and visual-design preparation establish the barrier and are therefore eligible before approval.

For command syntax, rule limits and current resumption behavior, read the `cis agent run` and `cis agent resume` manuals from the CIS distribution.
